Append-Only Audit History

Append-Only Audit History

Understand how committed audit events are preserved and later corrections are recorded without rewriting the original logical history.

Status

FinKore Core 2.0.5 stable.

Purpose

This document defines logical preservation rules for committed Audit Events, independently of physical storage technology.

Requirements

  • AUDIT-APPEND-001 — Within logical audit history, a committed Audit Event MUST NOT be replaced, modified, or removed. A policy-authorized redacted representation follows Audit Redaction and MUST leave evidence of the redaction.
    Evidence & context3 research notes+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Illustrates a risk

    Timestamp precedence cannot replace the defined aggregation of effective approvals ↗

    Abhilash Katari

    When opposing decisions remain valid and effective, defined aggregation and preserved history govern the result. A later timestamp alone is neither withdrawal nor supersession; LWW is not universally prohibited.

    Scope and limitations

    The example assumes both opposing Decisions are valid and still effective. Legitimate withdrawal/supersession differs from timestamp overwrite. LWW may still suit a cache or application value whose declared semantics permit it.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Preserving collected traces does not prove capture of required events ↗

    Surendra Kumar Valavala

    Domain event identity, complete event fields and preservation of committed records do not demonstrate capture of every required occurrence. The conceptual framework motivates an independent coverage question.

    Scope and limitations

    A separate expected workload can test coverage if it is independent of the collector. This is not a mandate to record every request or collect sensitive content indiscriminately. A diagnostic retry trace is not itself a unique financial effect.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Convergence does not by itself promise permanence after a response ↗

    Dina Borrego; Nuno Preguiça; Elisa Gonzalez Boix; Carla Ferreira

    The source explicitly permits discarding some operations after a response. That tradeoff does not authorize erasing committed history or rewriting preserved source facts; portable reversal requires its declared evidence. Distributed confirmation and concrete accounting consequences remain separate.

    Scope and limitations

    An external action triggered by a later-discarded result is reviewer inference. A clearly provisional response may be appropriate. The source explicitly acknowledges the limitation; this review does not declare its framework generally unsuitable or its proofs invalid.

  • AUDIT-APPEND-002 — An ordering relationship explicitly recorded as part of committed logical history MUST NOT later be changed.
  • AUDIT-APPEND-003 — Submission of an already committed Audit Event identity MUST fail with FINKORE_AUDIT_DUPLICATE_EVENT and MUST NOT create another committed event.
    Evidence & context2 research notes · 1 practitioner account+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Idempotent request identity includes content and an explicitly bounded effect ↗

    Mikhaylov Bogdan; Omorov Akzholbek; Izripov Iusup

    These boundaries distinguish non-mutating domain rejection and duplicate-event rejection from a general command-key/retry protocol. The source’s request identity recommendation remains application policy.

    Scope and limitations

    Reviewer scenario: a lost response leads to retrying with the same key but a changed amount. Treating this as the same financial instruction can suppress a legitimate change or misidentify the result. Atomic key storage is the paper’s design; a key alone does not coordinate every external effect.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Producer idempotence does not settle application-effect uniqueness ↗

    Jyothirmai Gurramula

    Duplicate Audit identity rejection and conflict preconditions have bounded domain meaning. Producer guarantees and application-effect uniqueness need their own scope; no broker protocol, cached result or end-to-end exactly-once guarantee is supplied.

    Scope and limitations

    The crash-after-effect-before-acknowledgement scenario is reviewer inference. Broker guarantees have a useful defined scope. Application deduplication still needs defined keys, retention, durable recovery and a consistent effect boundary; the abstract does not establish those details.

    Legacy / Clarifies a boundary

    Retrying a batch is not evidence that each economic effect occurs only once ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Rejecting an already committed Audit Event identity prevents another committed event for that identity; it does not deduplicate a payment instruction.

    Scope and limitations

    This is a reported operational tendency, not proof that every retry duplicates payments. A retry after an uncertain outcome, a domain rejection and a new economic instruction are different cases. Concrete payment posting, batch scheduling, reconciliation and distributed effect coordination are outside the current Core contract. No idempotency key scheme, retention period or payment operation is prescribed.

  • AUDIT-APPEND-004 — Any exceptional transformation required by law or policy MUST remain detectable through compliant redaction evidence.
  • FinKore Core does not guarantee a total ordering of independently produced concurrent Audit Events.
  • AUDIT-APPEND-006 — When timestamps do not establish a reliable ordering between independently produced Audit Events, an implementation MUST NOT assign domain meaning to their arbitrary storage or retrieval order.

Invariants

Reading logical history later must preserve the existence and identity of every committed Audit Event, every explicitly recorded ordering relationship, and every committed Audit Relationship. A redacted representation must preserve the event-level meaning required by Audit Redaction.

Invalid Examples

  • Editing yesterday's event to match a later value.
  • Deleting a rejected decision after a later approval.
  • Treating database row order as proof that one concurrent event caused another.

Errors

An attempted prohibited mutation must report FINKORE_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY_VIOLATION.

Open Questions

  • Should a future specification define entity-local sequencing or explicit causal relationships between Audit Events?

Non-Goals

This document does not prescribe event stores, ledgers, hashes, signatures, replication protocols, global sequence numbers, Lamport clocks, vector clocks, broker offsets, distributed consensus, or database transaction ordering. Entity Evolution operation semantics are defined outside Audit; Audit Relationships only preserve evidence links.
